### Get started

Starting today, Gemini 4 Argon is available in Gemini for business on the web, desktop, and mobile. Enterprise developers and builders can access Argon via API in Gemini platform under model ID `gemini-4-argon`, in Google AI Studio, and in Google Antigravity.

results.title: What’s new in AI infrastructure this month | Google Cloud Blog
results.author: Alex Barrett, Dave Bartoletti
highlights:
What’s new in AI infrastructure and orchestration in October

October 30, 2026

...

- New compute service: Agent Compute Engine is a purpose-built compute service providing high-performance, hardware-isolated microVM sandboxes alongside expanded agent governance capabilities like Agent Gateway and Agent Registry, all in the service of securing and scaling autonomous AI agents. Its primary benefits include rapid sub-second activation, extreme workload density through copy-on-write memory sharing, enterprise-grade security and identity management, and cross-cloud observability.
- AI Hypercomputer updates: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin 2026 we announced updates to our agentic infrastructure, including to A5X instances powered by the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, Virgo Network scale-out fabric, and Managed Lustre storage. These co-engineered advancements provide enterprises with accelerated performance, enhanced sovereign AI controls, while advanced Confidential Computing capabilities help you train and deploy complex multi-step models securely and efficiently.
- GKE product update: CPU startup boost for GKE, in preview, uses Kubernetes In-place Pod Resize to dynamically elevate container CPU resources during initialization and scale them back down to steady-state levels without having to restart the containers. This feature removes startup throttling and accelerates cold starts by up to 2x for demanding workloads, helping to lower cloud infrastructure costs.
- GKE product update: The preview of the Wiz Runtime Sensor add-on for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) brings low-touch deployment, automated lifecycle management, enterprise credential security, and fleet-wide governance to Wiz's eBPF runtime threat detection for both Standard and Autopilot GKE clusters.
- Modernization tools: Together at last. Google Cloud Modernize brings Google Cloud’s migration and modernization tools, including Migration Center, Google Cloud VMware Engine, Google Cloud Mainframe Modernization and our new EKS-to-GKE Migration Agent, into a single portfolio. Enterprise teams now have purpose-built agentic capabilities across infrastructure assessment, platform modernization, and application modernization.
- Cloud Run product update: Temporal Serverless Workers on Cloud Run automatically scale worker pools based on Temporal task queue demands and scale down to zero when idle. This integration eliminates cluster management, lowers costs, using Temporal Worker Versioning to safely handle stateful, long-running workflows and AI agent workloads.
- New open-source product: llm-d 1.0 is an open-source, Kubernetes-native serving stack that turns a cluster of model servers into a coordinated serving pool, unifying distributed LLM inference across mixed Google Cloud TPU and GPU fleets. Co-founded by Google and partners, it provides production-ready benefits such as cache-aware routing, tiered KV cache offloading, and priority-based flow control to dramatically improve context reuse, reduce time-to-first-token latency, and efficiently scale multi-tenant agent workloads.
- New open-source product: Working with Meta, we open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch stack that integrates Google TPUs directly into the PyTorch ecosystem alongside GPUs and CPUs. Now developers can train, serve, and deploy models natively on TPUs using familiar frameworks like Hugging Face, vLLM, and TorchTitan.
- Google Distributed Cloud updates: Organizations that operate under strict sovereignty mandates would love to use AI to help them process data, but can’t send it to the cloud. The latest version of Google Distributed Cloud (GDC) air-gapped brings frontier AI models and multimodal enterprise search with Gemini into these isolated environments. In addition, GDC air-gapped supports NVIDIA HGX B300 systems based on the NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra architecture, and features enhanced networking and security capabilities. 
- Edge inference product: Google open-sourced ML Drift, a cross-platform on-device GPU compute engine built for LiteRT that abstracts hardware complexities across OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. The framework delivers peak performance, enhanced 5D tensor support, and memory efficiency for both classical machine learning workloads and advanced generative AI models at the edge.
- Open-weight model support: Reflection's Beam is an open-weight, 501-parameter model released under an Apache 2.0 license designed specifically for frontier software engineering and long-horizon agentic tasks. We announced day 0 support and ready-to-run deployment recipes for service Beam on AI Hypercomputer and NVIDIA AI Infrastructure.

...

- Google is a leader in The Forrester Wave™: Public Cloud Platforms, Q3 2026: Highest overall score of any cloud provider!
- Google named a Leader in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Strategic Cloud Platform Services: Positioned furthest for “Completeness of Vision” of all vendors evaluated.
- Google is a Leader in the 2026 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Container Management: Positioned highest in “Ability to Execute” of all vendors evaluated.
- Google Cloud achieved a Gold rating in the latest SemiAnalysis ClusterMax 3.0 report, which evaluates the reliability, performance, support, pricing, and security of GPU providers globally. See the full report for more.

...

- Product update: Filestore, Google Cloud’s first-party, secure, scalable NFS file service, has emerged as a popular storage platform for AI and agentic workflows, and now, it’s even better suited to the task, with a new backend storage layer built directly on Colossus, Google’s foundational distributed storage system. This new backend lets you provision IOPS independently from storage capacity, and is deeply integrated with GKE. In AI environments, this can help you service so-called agentic swarms — large groups of agents that need to read and write to a common dataset — without a drop off in performance. For more, check out the blog post. 
- New feature: gVisor sandboxes are now available in distributed Ray clusters on GKE. In partnership with Anyscale, we introduced an experimental library for Ray that brings gVisor, Google’s open-source application kernel, directly into distributed Ray clusters. gVisor provides lightweight environments with stronger isolation than ordinary containers, plus fast startup times and low memory overhead. To try out these sandboxing capabilities on GKE, head over to the Ray sandboxing User Guide.
- Product update: Looking for high-performance, easy-to-use infrastructure on which to run a personal AI agent, but don’t want to spend a lot of money? New Cloud Run instances are dedicated, singleton compute runtimes on Cloud Run that won’t shut down when the agent is idle. Better yet, the cost to run a Cloud Run instance with 1 vCPU and 1 GiB of memory continuously for 30 days is just $5.70.

...

- Product update: Protecting sensitive data used with AI is a critical part of advanced and secure cloud infrastructure. Confidential Computing cryptographically protects data in use in hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) with verifiable data integrity, and is now available on the accelerator-optimized G4 machine series, featuring NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. Get started with Confidential G4 VMs and Confidential G4 GKE Nodes.
- Developer resource: The new TPU Developer Hub is the place to go for model builders, optimizers, and developers to learn to unlock the full performance of Google Cloud TPUs. Read more in this blog. 
- New product: Scale your AI workloads with the new OpenTelemetry-Based TPU AI Telemetry Collector Agent. For the first time, you can route high-fidelity TPU hardware telemetry to Google Cloud Monitoring, Google Managed Prometheus, or your own self-hosted Grafana stack.

results.title: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash now GA: cost-effective video | Google Cloud Blog
highlights:
Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash: Fast, cost-effective, and reliable video generation and editing now generally available

November 5, 2026

##### John Nack

Sr. Product Manager

Today, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash is generally available on Google Cloud. Built for the everyday videos businesses make in volume — like product videos, virtual try-ons, and ads — this model is fast, cost-effective, and follows your image, video and audio references more closely than before. 

Business users can create with it in Gemini for business and Google Vids, and developers can build with it via API.

Here's what's new:

- A lower price: $0.07 per second of 720p video, 30% less than Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, with similar savings at other resolutions.
- Longer clips: Generate and edit videos of up to 15 seconds, up from 10s.
- More consistent results: stronger adherence to image and video references keeps products, characters, and brand details consistent from shot to shot.
- Faster drafts, in higher resolution: create drafts at 360p or 720p, then upscale the best creations to 1080p or 4K.
- More natural speech: You can generate scenes with more fluid, natural-sounding dialogue, clearer lip-sync, and distinct multi-speaker conditioning.
- Editing in conversation: refine the same clip, such as swapping a product, changing lighting, or changing camera angle, instead of starting over.

Note: Audio references are gated behind allowlisting.

results.title: Confidential G4 GPUs are GA | Google Cloud Blog
highlights:
Confidential G4 GPUs are GA | Google Cloud Blog

Hardware-backed security at global scale: Confidential G4 with NVIDIA Blackwell is GA

October 21, 2026

##### Meghna Sreenivasan

Product Manager, Confidential Computing

##### Sam Lugani

Product Lead, Confidential Computing

##### The Future of AI Infrastructure

See how co-designed, open systems scale AI on November 9

Bringing autonomous agents into production means processing sensitive data and valuable intellectual property in real time. Protecting proprietary model weights, user prompts, and generated outputs requires security that safeguards data while it is actively being computed.

As part of our efforts to enable your enterprise securely, today we are announcing that Confidential Computing on Google Cloud’s G4 instances enabled by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server edition GPUs is now generally available. This release integrates NVIDIA Confidential Computing directly into Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer, delivering the dynamic performance needed to scale without compromising privacy.

When we announced Confidential G4 in preview earlier this year, we talked about its global footprint and scale. Today, these instances are generally available across 36 zones, using multiple consumption models, on Compute Engine VMs and GKE nodes.

In addition, support for Confidential Space enabling secure multi-party data sharing is rolling out to general availability in the coming weeks.

...

Protecting data in use shouldn't mean sacrificing GPU throughput or operational agility. By combining non-exportable hardware keys, verifiable remote attestation, and transparent memory encryption, Confidential G4 helps organizations maximize their investments in agentic and inference workloads. Enterprises can keep costs low while meeting strict regulatory and compliance requirements.

results.title: Storage-optimized Z4M machine series are GA | Google Cloud Blog
highlights:
November 6, 2026

##### bob Napaa

Today, we’re excited to announce the general availability of our next-generation Storage-optimized Z4M machine series in Google Compute Engine, available as both Virtual Machine (VM) and bare-metal instances. 

We built Z4M to provide storage for AI/ML training and inference workloads such as checkpointing, distributed key-value (KV) cache and parallel file systems — workloads that handle huge data volumes and require massive parallel data processing, as well as high storage and networking throughput. Low latency access to data is equally critical to keep GPUs and TPUs fully utilized. Powered by the fifth-generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors and paired with the latest enhancements in Titanium, Z4M provides up to 168,000 GiB of Local SSD (LSSD) storage coupled with up to 400 Gbps of Cloud Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) networking. RDMA improves the performance of these demanding workloads by reducing data-access latency by up to 60% compared to TCP networking, so you can increase your applications’ throughput while right-sizing your cloud investment.

results.author: Andrea Morange
highlights:

AI Hypercomputer: Designed specifically for demanding AI workloads, our AI Hypercomputer is an advanced, purpose-built architecture that unites performance-optimized hardware for compute, storage, networking, open software and machine learning frameworks — as well as flexible consumption models — into a single, integrated system. We are announcing innovations at every layer of the AI Hypercomputer:

- TPU 8t, optimized for training, uses breakthrough Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) technology to scale up to 9,600 TPUs and 2 PB of shared, high-bandwidth memory in a single superpod. It achieves 3x the processing power of Ironwood and delivers up to 2x more performance/Watt. 
- TPU 8i, optimized for inference, uses our new Boardfly topology to directly connect 1,152 TPUs in a single pod. It features 3x more on-chip SRAM compared to previous versions to host larger KV caches entirely on-silicon and integrates a specialized Collectives Acceleration Engine. Taken together, TPU 8i delivers 80% better performance per dollar for inference than the prior generation, enabling millions of concurrent agents to run cost-effectively.

##### Mark Lohmeyer

November 6, 2026: A5X Instances are now generally available

capabilities

- Accelerated computing with A5X instances based on NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform: These bare-metal GPU-accelerated instances feature the latest NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform to deliver performance at scale. With general availability, coming next month, we are also expanding our infrastructure footprint to support EMEA data residency and sovereignty requirements with availability in new local regions. 
- Scale-out A5X networking with Virgo Network: Virgo Network supports a non-blocking intra- and inter-building scale-out fabric via mesh topology. This new capability will enable extreme horizontal scaling, allowing clusters to expand to 80,000 Rubin GPUs within a single site and up to 960,000 Rubin GPUs across multi-site deployments.
- Storage with Managed Lustre and NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage: Google Cloud Managed Lustre will support NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage on A5X instances, giving training and inference data a direct RDMA path from the parallel file system into GPU memory, bypassing the CPU and system memory. 
- Long-context memory with KV Caching: A5X instances will also support advanced KV-caching capabilities designed to scale context memory beyond GPU high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for long-context and multi-turn agentic workloads. This high-speed caching layer will offload and reuse context across storage tiers, reducing redundant computation, lowering time-to-first-token, and improving inference goodput per dollar.
- Workload orchestration with A5X instances on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE brings a suite of features for distributed AI workloads, such as GKE Managed DRANET, which simplifies RDMA management by making network interface cards first-class native Kubernetes resources; and Kueue, which boosts performance of distributed workloads through topology-aware scheduling and resource management. This makes GKE and A5X instances a powerful combination for agentic workload orchestration.

...

- NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs on GDC: Following our preview announced earlier this year, the latest NVIDIA HGX B300 systems are now generally available (GA) on GDC. This brings industry-leading compute density and energy efficiency on-premises, providing the high-throughput platform foundation that demanding local inference workloads require.
- Gemini Flash models on GDC: We are expanding our sovereign model catalog with Gemini 3.5 Flash on GDC, accelerated by NVIDIA HGX B300. Organizations can now execute rapid, high-throughput multimodal reasoning, spanning text, audio, video, and imagery, entirely inside their air-gapped perimeter.
- Enterprise search capabilities on GDC: Available in preview, our enterprise search capabilities with Gemini on GDC air-gapped delivers an out-of-the-box conversational interface powered by multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). These capabilities are powered by Gemini on GDC air-gapped with NVIDIA HGX B300. Now, analysts and knowledge workers can instantly query, summarize, and cross-examine proprietary documents, media, and unstructured archives without custom engineering, keeping all indexing, embeddings, and interactions strictly within your sovereign security boundary.

Today, we’re announcing the general availability of an Anthropic-managed deployment option for Claude Models on Google Cloud. This gives teams more choice in how they run their models, helping them consolidate AI workloads on Google Cloud alongside our existingGoogle-managed deployment option. 

Both options deliver the same frontier models on day zero, the same pricing, and the same Google Cloud billing. The difference comes down to who acts as your data processor and whether you need access to the new Claude platform features when they launch:

...

Continues to deliver day-zero access to the latest Claude models with strict governance, compliance, and sovereignty requirements. Google Cloud operates as the data processor under existing customer agreements, providing VPC Service Controls, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK), and data residency in the U.S., EU, and APAC. New Claude Platform features roll out over time as they are integrated into the Google-managed infrastructure. Teams also benefit from native integrations with Google Cloud services like BigQuery and Model Armor, along with standard billing and eligible commitment drawdown. 

### Comparing deployment options

| Feature | Anthropic-managed | Google-managed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model availability | Available on Day 0 | Available on Day 0 |
| First-party tools and betas | Available on Day 0 | Available once integrated into the Google-managed infrastructure |
| Data processor and terms | Anthropic (under Anthropic’s Commercial Terms) | Google Cloud (under existing Google Cloud customer agreements) |
| Pricing & commitments | Standard pricing (draws down eligible Google Cloud commitments) | |
